title: On one GOES flux scale, Cycle 25 regions give 1.6 times more M flares than Cycle 24 regions of the same McIntosh and magnetic class (1998-2026); HMI magnetic parameters reduce this to 1.1-1.2
abstract: Question: on the homogeneous (science) GOES flux scale, Solar Cycle 25 has about 1.45 times more M flares per sunspot than Cycle 24 but not more per F10.7 unit. Is this a change in the mix of sunspot groups or a higher flare rate per region? Method: we attributed SWPC flares with true-scale peaks (prior SCI list) to 45,202 SWPC Solar Region Summary region-days (1998-2026) and to 19,838 HMI SHARP HARP-days (2010-2026). We compared Cycle 25 and Cycle 24 rates at matched McIntosh class, magnetic class and area, and at matched SHARP parameters, with 27-day block-bootstrap intervals. Results: with Cycle 24 class rates, the expected Cycle 25 rate per sunspot number is 0.96 (0.82-1.11) times the Cycle 24 value, so composition does not explain the excess. At matched class, Cycle 25 regions produce 1.61 (1.32-1.99) times more M1+ flares on the true scale and 2.44 (1.97-3.02) on the operational list. The ratio is 1.44-1.80 in all sensitivity variants. It is 1.24 (0.88-1.74) for M5+ and 1.16 (0.70-2.06) for X1+ flares. At the same SRS class, Cycle 25 regions have 1.05 times more unsigned flux, 1.06 times more current helicity and 0.14 dex more polarity-inversion-line flux (R_VALUE). At matched SHARP parameters, the Cycle 25/24 ratio is 1.13-1.22 (four parameters: 1.22, 1.05-1.46). Cycle 25 has 1.16 (1.09-1.25) times more SHARP flux per sunspot number. Thus sunspot-based indices under-count the flare-relevant magnetic flux of Cycle 25. Class-based flare rates trained on pre-2020 operational classes under-predict Cycle 25 operational M rates by about 2.4. Limitations: three cycles (one incomplete), subjective SRS classes, 15-27% of flares not attributed to a same-day region, a small SRS-HMI subsample, and internal checks of HMI stability only.
